summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the Changed series with part five, Change My Mouth. The service opened with a welcome, a testimony from a man whose life was transformed after giving his life to Jesus and being baptized alongside his wife, and a weekly declaration rooted in 2 Corinthians 5:17: if anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation. Pastor Travis then compared the destructive power of the world's most feared weapons with something far more common, the human mouth. Words can wound marriages, discourage children, and leave lasting emotional scars. They can also lift up, encourage, and even lead people to Jesus. Drawing on Proverbs 18:21, he taught that the tongue holds the power of life and death, that our mouths are never neutral, and that our words are seeds that eventually grow into the world we live in.

Pastor Travis shared four keys. First, we are responsible to guard our mouths. Using Proverbs 21:23 and James 1, he encouraged the church to be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry. He also urged us to filter our words by asking whether they are true, necessary, helpful, and loving, including what we write in texts and online. Second, our mouths reveal our hearts. Using the picture of a cup of coffee bumped in a busy lobby, he explained that pressure does not put anything inside us, it only reveals what is already there. Jesus said in Luke 6:45 that the mouth speaks what the heart is full of, so lasting change is not simple behavior modification but God working from the inside out. Third, some words do not belong in a changed life: gossip, slander, lying, and profanity. Ephesians 4:29 calls believers to speak only what builds others up, and Proverbs 12:18 and 15:4 contrast reckless words with words that bring healing. Fourth, we are invited to consecrate our mouths to God, setting them apart for his use so that our words become worship. James 3 reminds us that praise and cursing should not flow from the same mouth.

Pastor Travis closed with a practical challenge: commit to thirty days without profanity, lying, or gossip, and invite a trusted friend to offer loving accountability, remembering that we will give an account for our words (Matthew 12). He also pointed to Romans 10:9-10, which shows that our words can confess Jesus as Lord. He invited anyone who had not yet surrendered to Christ to confess him and receive salvation. The message is both sobering and hopeful: a changed heart produces changed words, and changed words can help change the world around us.
mainPoints: Our words carry the power of life and death, so we are responsible to guard our mouths by listening more, speaking carefully, and filtering what we say and write.
Our mouths reveal what is stored in our hearts, so lasting change comes from God transforming us from the inside out, not from behavior modification alone.
A changed life leaves behind gossip, slander, lying, and profanity, and consecrates the mouth to God so our words build others up and become worship.

versesMentioned.text: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

If you declare with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For it is with your heart that you believe and are justified, and it is with your mouth that you profess your faith and are saved.
Those who guard their mouths and their tongues keep themselves from calamity.
Those who consider themselves religious and yet do not keep a tight rein on their tongues deceive themselves, and their religion is worthless.
My dear brothers and sisters, take note of this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from telling lies.
A good man brings good things out of the good stored up in his heart, and an evil man brings evil things out of the evil stored up in his heart. For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.
Here is a trustworthy saying that deserves full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.
I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do I do not do, but what I hate I do.
What shall we say, then? Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase?
If you love me, keep my commands.
For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.

Likewise, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark. The tongue also is a fire, a world of evil among the parts of the body. It corrupts the whole body, sets the whole course of one's life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
Do not let any unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building others up according to their needs, that it may benefit those who listen.
You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.

You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, not holding to the truth, for there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, for he is a liar and the father of lies.
Jesus answered, "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me."
The soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
The words of the reckless pierce like swords, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

With the tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings, who have been made in God's likeness. Out of the same mouth come praise and cursing. My brothers and sisters, this should not be. Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring? My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree bear olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
But I tell you that everyone will have to give account on the day of judgment for every empty word they have spoken. For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.

Monday.scripture: Proverbs 21:23 (NIV): "Those who guard their mouths and their tongues keep themselves from calamity."
Monday.action: Before sending any text, email, or social media post today, pause for a few seconds and ask: Is it true? Is it necessary? Is it helpful? Is it loving? If not, do not send it.
Monday.prayer: Lord, help me guard my mouth and my messages today. Give me wisdom to pause before I speak or write, and let my words reflect you. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: James 1:19 (NIV): "Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry."
Tuesday.action: In at least two conversations today, listen fully without interrupting. Wait a moment before you respond, and ask one caring question.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, make me quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry. Help me value the people in front of me. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Luke 6:45 (NIV): "For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of."
Wednesday.action: Take five quiet minutes to notice what tends to spill out of you when you are stressed (worry, anger, complaint, or gossip). Write it down and ask God to change what is inside, not just what comes out.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, search my heart. Show me what is stored there that needs your healing and change. Fill me with your peace, praise, and love. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Ephesians 4:29 (NIV): "Do not let any unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building others up according to their needs."
Thursday.action: Send one sincere message of encouragement or gratitude to a family member, friend, or coworker, and offer one kind word to someone in person.
Thursday.prayer: God, let my words be a source of life to others today. Show me who needs encouragement, and give me the right words to say. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Psalm 34:13 (NIV): "Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from telling lies."
Friday.focus: Setting aside gossip, lying, and unwholesome talk
Friday.action: Begin a 30-day commitment to avoid profanity, lying, and gossip. Ask a trusted friend or family member to lovingly hold you accountable, and if someone begins to gossip today, kindly change the subject.
Friday.prayer: Lord, I commit my words to you for the next 30 days. Give me strength and humility, and help me to be honest and kind in everything I say. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: James 3:9-10 (NIV): "With the tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings, who have been made in God's likeness. Out of the same mouth come praise and cursing."
Saturday.action: Set aside time to praise God out loud through worship music or prayer. Then reflect on the week, thank God for progress, and decide to set your mouth apart for his use again tomorrow.
Saturday.prayer: Father, my mouth belongs to you. Let every word be an act of worship that honors you and blesses others. Thank you for changing my heart. Amen.

title: How to Control Your Tongue and Change Your Life | Changed, Part 5
